items.text: @Marcus Bell flagging FRAUD-2291. A $48k inbound wire landed this morning from a Cyprus entity, Coastal Meridian Trading Ltd, which looks a lot like a shell (no web presence, generic trading name). It went into a wealth account opened only in the last couple of months, and the money is already being split into sub-$10k internal transfers. Do you want me to put a hold on the account before the weekend?

Not yet. I don't want to freeze a client account on a single wire and a hunch, and we'd need more than this to defend a hold. Can you map where every dollar went and check whether the receiving accounts are connected to each other? Write it up early next week and we'll decide from there.

items.title: FRAUD-2291 preliminary review
items.text:
Hi Marcus,

Here is my preliminary write-up on FRAUD-2291 (FraudScore transaction t_r016), following your note in #compliance on Friday. It covers the money trail only. The connection analysis is still outstanding (see Next steps).

Summary
The pattern looks like layering through a newly opened wealth account. There are four phases.

1. August: structured funding. Through August the account received a string of ACH credits, each kept under $10,000. None of them tripped a CTR-style threshold on its own, but the cadence and the near-identical amounts look deliberate. Taken together they don't match the funding profile captured at onboarding.

2. Sep 25: the inbound wire. At 10:14 ET a $48,000.00 inbound wire arrived from Coastal Meridian Trading Ltd (Cyprus). That is the transaction FraudScore flagged. I found nothing tying the originator to the client's stated source of wealth or occupation.

3. Sep 25-28: internal transfers. Within hours the funds started moving to several other Halcyon accounts in internal book transfers. Every one was under $10,000, mostly in the $9,200-$9,900 range. Almost all of the $48k had left the original account within about three business days.

4. Sep 29-30: outbound wires to crypto. On Sep 29 and Sep 30 the receiving accounts sent outgoing wires through PaymentsGateway to Bitrail Digital Exchange, a US crypto exchange, beneficiary account {{CP_ACCOUNT:cp_063}}. Several separate Halcyon accounts all wiring to the same exchange beneficiary within a two-day window is the part that concerns me most.

What I have not done yet
I have not checked whether the receiving accounts share phone numbers, home addresses, or login devices. That is my next step. I plan to pull the ClientHub contact records and the online banking session and device data for each account. If they overlap, we are probably looking at a coordinated ring rather than one bad actor.

Assessment
The sequence fits a classic placement-layering pattern: structured deposits, a large offshore wire, fragmentation under $10k, then exit to crypto. I think a SAR is likely here, but I want the connection analysis done before we commit to a narrative.

Ask
Can I have your approval to formally escalate this? That would mean opening a case in AMLMonitor and pulling in the RMs on the affected accounts on a need-to-know basis. Jenna, I've copied you because I'll need help extracting the session and device data for the linkage work. I also want to confirm that the FraudScore rules would catch a repeat of this pattern.

Thanks,
Nadia
